reason: The 1976-77 founding cannot be told as a documented episode. Loadable sources (Bloomberg's 2013 profile via The National, Irish Farmers Journal 2013, an Arab News PR-based piece, Otago Daily Times) give only bare facts: founded 1977 (or 1976) by Prince Sultan bin Mohammed bin Saud Al Kabeer with the McGuckians' Masstock, amid a 1970s food-security push, starting with fresh milk and laban, centralised to four Al Kharj farms in the early 1990s, Masstock exiting in 2004. None describes the founders' decision, what they knew, the first farm or early setbacks, and there is no founder interview. The fuller accounts (Irish Embassy biography of Alastair McGuckian, DFA 2015 release, The Currency 2026) are blocked (403) or paywalled; Almarai's own history pages render only with JavaScript. The founding date itself conflicts (May 1976 per the Irish Embassy; 1977 elsewhere). Later well-reported episodes (fodder imports, Fondomonte in Argentina and Arizona) are company decisions with no documented founder role. Five searches used.
